description: Detect the terminal's inline autosuggestion (greyed ghost text) so the phone's accept-autocomplete button only activates when there is actually a suggestion to accept, and the Mac never injects Right-arrow into empty air. Pure ANSI-parsing lives in a Foundation-only Shared detector gated by a swiftc assertion harness (tools/run-autosuggest-tests.sh); the Mac broadcast flag + iOS button gating + Mac inject guard are grep-verified in the loop and integration-built by a human.

userStories.title: Detect inline autosuggestion from content
userStories.description: As a Quip developer, I want a Foundation-only helper that reports the inline ghost-text suggestion on the terminal's input line, so both peers can tell whether there is anything to accept before showing or sending the accept-autocomplete action.
acceptanceCriteria: Create Shared/AutosuggestDetector.swift (import Foundation only, no AppKit/UIKit/SwiftUI) exposing AutosuggestDetector.suggestionText(in content: String) -> String? and AutosuggestDetector.hasSuggestion(in content: String) -> Bool.

suggestionText inspects only the LAST non-empty line of content and returns the ANSI-stripped text of a TRAILING run styled dim/faint (SGR 2) or grey foreground (SGR 90, or 8-bit greys 38;5;8 and 38;5;236..245) that is immediately preceded on that line by NON-dim text (the user's typed input); it returns nil otherwise.
A dim run that spans the WHOLE line (no non-dim typed prefix) returns nil, and dim text on any line other than the last non-empty line returns nil (scrollback must not trigger).
Content with no ANSI escapes, empty content, and screenshot-mode/plain content all return nil; hasSuggestion returns suggestionText(in:) != nil.
Create tools/run-autosuggest-tests.sh that compiles Shared/AutosuggestDetector.swift plus a Foundation-only assertion harness with swiftc and runs it, exiting non-zero on any failed assertion.

The harness asserts: `you typed \u{1B}[2mghost text\u{1B}[0m` on the last line => suggestionText == "ghost text"; a fully-dim line => nil; a plain no-ANSI line => nil; dim text on an earlier line with a plain last line => nil.
bash tools/run-autosuggest-tests.sh exits 0 with all US-001 assertions passing.
userStories.notes: Shared/AutosuggestDetector.swift + tools/run-autosuggest-tests.sh; harness exits 0 (16 assertions incl. grey-fg variants, SGR 22 cancel, padding/newline edges).

userStories.title: Broadcast a per-window suggestion flag
userStories.description: As a Quip developer, I want the Mac to tell the phone whether each window currently shows an autosuggestion, so the phone can gate its accept button on live state rather than guessing.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a hasAutosuggest: Bool field to the per-window content/layout update the Mac broadcasts (the same message the phone renders InlineTerminalContent from), computed via AutosuggestDetector.hasSuggestion on that window's scraped content.
The new field decodes as false when absent so an older phone/Mac still decodes the message (back-compat, matching the additive-field pattern used for phonePrefsSnapshot).
The iOS model that receives the update exposes the flag to InlineTerminalContent without breaking existing rendering.
grep confirms the Mac sets hasAutosuggest from AutosuggestDetector and the iOS decode path carries it through.
bash tools/run-autosuggest-tests.sh exits 0 (US-001 harness still green).
Human integration gate noted: xcodebuild build QuipMac + QuipiOS (after xcodegen generate) succeeds.
userStories.notes: TerminalContentMessage.hasAutosuggest (custom init(from:) defaults false when absent); Mac computes isTerminal && AutosuggestDetector.hasSuggestion(in: redacted) at broadcast; iOS carries via WebSocketClient->BackendConnectionManager->QuipApp map->InlineTerminalContent(hasAutosuggest:). Both peers BUILD SUCCEEDED after xcodegen regen (pbxproj restored); MessageProtocolTests 95/0.

userStories.title: Gate the iOS accept button
userStories.description: As a Quip user, I want the accept-autocomplete button to be active only when a suggestion is actually showing, so tapping it never just nudges the cursor when there is nothing to accept.
acceptanceCriteria: In QuipiOS/QuipApp.swift InlineTerminalContent, the accept-autocomplete button (the text.append icon that sends press_right) is enabled/full-opacity only when the window's hasAutosuggest flag is true, and disabled/dimmed otherwise.
The button still sends the press_right quick-action when enabled; no new fixed row is added (compact-UI rule preserved).
When hasAutosuggest is false the button does not send press_right (guarded by .disabled or an early return).
grep confirms the button's enabled/opacity state is driven by hasAutosuggest.
bash tools/run-autosuggest-tests.sh exits 0 (US-001 harness still green).
Human UI gate noted: install QuipiOS and confirm the button greys out with no suggestion and accepts a live one.

userStories.title: Guard Right-arrow injection on live state
userStories.description: As a Quip user, I want the Mac to drop a stray accept tap when no suggestion is present at inject time, so a race between my tap and the screen never moves the cursor into my typed text.
acceptanceCriteria: Add AutosuggestDetector.shouldAccept(liveContent: String) -> Bool (returns hasSuggestion(in:)) as the pure decision the injector consults.

In QuipMac/QuipMacApp.swift handleQuickAction, the press_right case re-scrapes the focused window's live content and only calls sendKeystroke("right") when AutosuggestDetector.shouldAccept(liveContent:) is true; otherwise it skips injection (and may log the skip), mirroring how answerStillValid guards one-tap answers.
grep confirms the press_right path consults AutosuggestDetector before injecting.
The harness asserts shouldAccept is true for the ghost-text sample and false for a plain no-suggestion line.
bash tools/run-autosuggest-tests.sh exits 0 with all US-001..US-004 assertions passing.
Human integration gate noted: rebuild QuipMac and confirm a tap with no suggestion is a no-op while a tap with one accepts.
